items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: So, Dr. George Howard's daddy, he came to me one time, there was a political rally. And he came to me, heard me playing... They asked me that I'd like to come out with them and play.

ctx.x: Well, let me ask you this. What did you call this music? You didn't use the word ragtime, did you? You didn't call it ragtime, did you? Called it ragtime. You called it ragtime. When you were 14?

When you were 14? Yes. When I was 14, that was the name of that stuff. Ragtime. Ragtime. No other name. We used to play all that kind of humbug stuff with them picaloos and stuff, you understand? Yes. When I was 14. Mm-hmm. See? Well, it... It happened, we used to go around the street with a bunch of kids. Flags and torch lights and stuff like that playing. Every night we'd be out in the street playing music. And marching. Making money out of it? No. No, just having fun. Just for pleasure. Uh-huh. So, Dr. George…
Do you remember who was running for office?
